title: Simon's Algorithm
summary: Recover a hidden XOR mask from outcomes that are orthogonal to it.
objectives: Build Simon's circuit so that every measurement of the input register returns a string y with y·s = 0 (mod 2).
Collect several outcomes with run_shots and solve the linear system y·s = 0 modulo 2 to compute the hidden string s.
Explain why n − 1 independent equations determine s, and why s = 000 is recognized by the absence of a nonzero solution.
mission: The function f takes 3 bits to 3 bits and satisfies f(x) = f(y) if and only if y = x or y = x ⊕ s, for a hidden string s (possibly 000, when f is one-to-one). Call oracle(qc) once (input register: qubits 0 to 2, output register: qubits 3 to 5), measure the input register into bits 0 to 2, and use run_shots to collect outcomes. Then compute, from the outcomes alone, the bit string s_found equal to s. Qubit 0 is the last character of every string, so s = s2 s1 s0 and an outcome is y2 y1 y0.

prediction.question: For n = 3, how many linearly independent equations y·s = 0 (mod 2) are needed to determine a nonzero secret s?
prediction.explanation: The outcomes y lie in the subspace orthogonal to s, which has dimension n − 1 = 2. Two independent outcomes span it, and s is the only nonzero string orthogonal to both. One equation leaves 3 nonzero candidates. A third independent equation would force s = 000.

hints: Apply Hadamard gates to qubits 0 to 2 before and after oracle(qc), and leave qubits 3 to 5 in |0⟩. Finish with qc.measure([0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 2]) and counts = run_shots(qc).
Each key of counts is a string y2y1y0 with y·s = 0 (mod 2). Compute the inner product of two bit strings with bin(int(a, 2) & int(b, 2)).count("1") % 2.

Loop over the nonzero candidates "001", "010", …, "111" and keep those whose inner product with every key of counts is 0. If exactly one remains, it is s. If none remains, the outcomes span all strings, f is one-to-one and s = "000".

challenge.mission: Simon's problem with a compact oracle. The function f takes 3 bits to 2 bits and satisfies f(x) = f(y) if and only if y = x or y = x ⊕ s, for a hidden nonzero string s (s is never 000, because a function with 2 output bits cannot be one-to-one on 8 inputs). Use a circuit qc with 5 qubits (input register: qubits 0 to 2, output register: qubits 3 and 4) and 3 classical bits, call oracle(qc) once, measure the input register into bits 0 to 2, and store in s_found the string s computed from the outcomes. Qubit 0 is the last character of every string.
hints: The output register needs only n − 1 = 2 qubits here, so the circuit has 5 qubits, not 6.
The procedure is the same: Hadamard gates, one query, Hadamard gates, measure qubits 0 to 2.
Every outcome y satisfies y·s = 0 (mod 2). With a nonzero s the outcomes span a 2-dimensional space, so exactly one nonzero string is orthogonal to all of them.
